title: CLM-016: tiered model routing versus uniform judgment routing
description: Compares a tiered execution profile (economy, standard and judgment routes) against a profile that sends every tier to the judgment route. Model ids in the profiles are placeholders.

hypothesis.statement: Reasoning budget, autonomy, and review intensity should be tiered by ambiguity, consequence of error, and checkability rather than maximized uniformly.
hypothesis.falsifier: A tiered execution profile does not lower provider cost per passed task compared with running every node at the judgment tier, or it lowers the pass rate by more than the run-to-run spread.

arms.label: Tiered routing
arms.description: Economy, standard and judgment routes. Pricing is a PLACEHOLDER list price in USD per million tokens (input 2.50, cached input 0.25, output 10.00); replace it with the current published prices of the model under study before interpreting estimated_cost.

arms.label: Uniform judgment routing
arms.description: Every tier uses the judgment route. Pricing is a PLACEHOLDER list price in USD per million tokens (input 2.50, cached input 0.25, output 10.00); replace it with the current published prices of the model under study before interpreting estimated_cost.
